thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected on prod-inference (service=inference-runtime). p99=3200ms, p95=900ms, SLO p99=1200ms. Streaming stalls reported. Auto-page sent.

sam_oncall: seeing it too, dashboards show a sudden jump around 13:42 UTC. Streaming responses stall at token ~120-140.

michelle_sre: confirmed. KV cache eviction rate spiked 20x on shard-17. Prefill traffic looks heavy vs decode threads.

ajay_runtime: logs show repeated prefill->decode handoff timeouts: `prefill_wait_ms` spikes to 1.8s. Might be fragment collisions on slab allocator.

jordan_prod: any customer-facing impact? CS getting a couple complaints about timeouts for chat streaming.

leo_support: two customers reported degraded streaming and partial responses, no data loss. Support ticket IDs: #6543, #6546. Notified accounts team.

sam_oncall: quick mitigation idea: throttle prefill sampling window to reduce concurrent prefill pressure, and enable aggressive KV eviction smoothing. Can someone flip the prefills limiter?

ajay_runtime: I can toggle limiter on the population service. Command: `POST /admin/config/prefill_rate_limit {"rate": 0.6}`. Will do in ~2m after snapshotting metrics.

michelle_sre: also propose enabling slab padding on affected nodes to reduce fragmentation: set `SLAB_PADDING=1.2` via feature-flip for pool-prod-17. That'll reduce collisions but increases memory usage.

ops-bot: Snapshot created: metrics_snapshot_4209991234 saved to /snapshots/4209991234.json by sam_oncall.

ajay_runtime: applying prefill rate change now -> `curl -X POST https://admin.prod/prefill -d '{"rate":0.6}'` -> 200.

sam_oncall: please monitor p99 and eviction rate.

michelle_sre: eviction rate dropping slowly. p99 down to ~2100ms after 2m. Prefill concurrency reduced ~40%. Streaming stall count down ~30%.

jordan_prod: pushing a temporary fallback policy for streaming: if token delay >1500ms, stream partial response and close; will that help?

ajay_runtime: can enable fallback at routing layer. Pushing config: `routes.streaming.fallback_timeout_ms=1500` -> applied.

leo_support: customers see improvements. Ticket #6543 updated: "observed improved streaming, will monitor".

michelle_sre: next steps: (1) run targeted slab defrag on pool-17 during low traffic window, (2) evaluate prefill batching changes to avoid head-of-line blocking, (3) long-term: adjust allocator to prefer decode allocations.

sam_oncall: I'm going to handoff to michelle for the overnight mitigation and monitoring. Leaving notes in PagerDuty and ops runbook.

michelle_sre: taking over. I'll schedule defrag at 02:10 UTC and keep prefill limiter at 0.6 until we validate allocator changes. If p99 > 1500ms for >15m, escalate to oncall@redwood-eng.

ajay_runtime: follow-up: captured `kv_stats` snapshot and upload link: https://internal.redwood/snapshots/4209991234/kv_stats.log. Shows fragmentation hotspots at segments 12/17/19.

ops-bot: Handoff logged: incident 4209991234 -> assignee michelle_sre. Handoff message appended to PD incident.

sam_oncall: thanks team. summary for postmortem: KV cache fragmentation + prefill/decode imbalance caused streaming tail latency spikes; mitigated by throttling prefill, enabling route fallback, and planned slab defrag. No customer data lost, limited customer impact, follow-up PM/eng review required.

michelle_sre: noted. I'll open a postmortem stub and attach snapshots + timeline.

jordan_prod: I'll coordinate customer communications for impacted accounts, linking to status page once incident marked resolved.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. If metrics remain stable for 30m mark resolved.

michelle_sre: monitoring OK at +25m, p99 ~980ms, streaming stalls near baseline. I'll keep watch and close after 30m.

leo_support: closing impacted tickets if no further reports after 1h.

michelle_sre: closing handoff in 10m, will publish postmortem draft tomorrow. Good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
